 :JUDGMENT:
This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.30,00,000/- for the death of Smt. Kempamma W/o Late Jogaiah in a Road Traffic accident.
2.

The substance of averments made in the Petition are as under:
SCCH 15 3 MVC No.3701/2023 That on 25.05.2023 at about 7.30 p.m., when the mother of the Petitioners by name Smt. Kempamma was proceeding as a pedestrian on extreme side of Harobele road, Uyyamballi Hobli, Kanakapura Taluk, at that time, one Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-2332 driven by its driver came in a very high speed and in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Smt. Kempamma.
Due to the said impact, the said Smt. Kempamma fell down and had sustained grievous injuries and died on the spot.
Thereafter, the Post mortem was conducted at Kanakapura Government Hospital and body was handed over to the Petitioners.
Prior to the date of the accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and she was a Homemaker and was earning a sum of Rs.18,000/- per month.
The Respondent No.1 is the owner and the Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-2332.
Therefore, the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

In pursuance of service of notice to the Respondents, both Respondents appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels and the Respondent No.2 filed its Objection Statement to the main petition.
Respondent No.1 did not choose to file Objection Statement.

The Respondent No.2 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and also denied the accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle and also the death of the Smt. Kempamma due to the injuries sustained in the said accident.
Further it admitted that the issuance of policy in respect of offending vehicle.

Further it contended that the driver of the offending vehicle was not holding valid and effective driving licence as on the date of accident and the owner had willfully entrusted the vehicle to the driver who did not hold DL.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.

sentences.text: Respondent No.2 has prayed to dismiss the petition against it.
On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:

ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Smt. Kempamma W/o Late Jogaiah was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 25.05.2023 at about 7.30 p.m., on Krishnaiahnadoddi village, Harobele road, Uyyamballi hobli, Kanakapura Taluk,
Ramangara District, due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-2332?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Smt. Kempamma?
3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?
If yes, what is the quantum and who is liable to pay?
4) What Order or Award?
5. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, the SCCH 15 6 MVC No.3701/2023 Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and got marked 16 documents at Ex.P.1 to 16.
Further, she examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked one document at Ex.P17 and closed her side evidence.
On the other hand, Respondent No.1 and 2 did not choose to lead evidence.

During the course of argument, the Learned Counsel for the Petitioners has relied on the decision reported in (2020) 11 Supreme Court Cases 356 in between National Insurance Company Limited Vs Birendra and Others and MFA No.2297/2018, between Mahadeva & others Vs. ICICI Lombard Motor Ins. Co. Ltd., and another 6.

sentences.text:
Having heard Arguments by both sides and upon perusal of the depositions, documents exhibited,
citations relied on and materials available on record, my answer to the above Issues are as under:
Issue No.1 : In the Affirmative Issue No.2 : In the Affirmative Issue No.3 : Partly in the Affirmative.
 Issue No.4 : As per the Final Order  SCCH 15 7 MVC No.3701/2023  for the following :
 REASONS Hema vs Anthony Kumar.J on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147122463/
3 7.

Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that their mother by name Smt.
Kempamma was died in the road traffic accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA- 10-A-2332.

8. On the other hand, the Respondent No.2 had denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-2332.
9.

In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.1 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the averments made in the petition.
10. The PW.1 has relied on Ex.P-1 to Ex.P16.

Ex.P-1 and 2 are the True copies of FIR and Complaint which shows that on the Complaint lodged by the son of the deceased i.e., Petitioner SCCH 15 8 MVC No.3701/2023 No.3, the Sathanoor Police have registered the case against the driver of Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-2332 for the offences punishable under Section 279,
304(A) and 427 of IPC and under Sec.187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P.3 is the Spot mahazar with Sketch which shows that the concerned police had drawn mahazar and sketch at the spot in the presence of panchas.
Ex.P-4 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not occurred due to any mechanical defects of the vehicle.
Ex.P5 is the Inquest Mahazar of the deceased.
Ex.P6 is the copy of PM report which shows the cause of death is due to shock and Haemorahage as a result head injury sustained.

Ex.P-7 is the true copy of the Charge-Sheet which shows that the I.O of the Sathanoor Police Station has submitted Charge-sheet against the driver of the offending Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA- 10-A-2332 for the offences punishable under Section 279, 304(A) and 427 of IPC and under Sec.187 of IMV Act.
Ex.P8 and 9 are the Police Notice and Reply.
Ex.P10 to 14 are the Aadhaar cards of the Petitioners and the deceased.
Ex.P15 is the School SCCH 15 9 MVC No.3701/2023 Certificate of the Petitioner No.3.
Ex.P16 is the Ration Card.
Further, Petitioner have examined one witness by name Kariyappa as PW.2 and got marked one document at Ex.P17.
He deposed that he has witnessed the accident.
But, in the Charge- sheet he was shown as Mahazar witness.
11. P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.2.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the contention of the Petitioners.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.1 and 2 did not choose to lead any oral or documentary evidence.

Hence,
the Respondent No.2 has failed to substantiate its Objection Statement contentions.

12. Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the case and evidence adduced by the Petitioners and documents exhibited, this Tribunal is of the opinion that the alleged accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-2332 SCCH 15 10 MVC No.3701/2023 and in the said accident, their mother was succumbed to the injuries.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is "In the Affirmative."

sentences.text: Issue No.2 and 3: Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid the repetition of facts.
14. The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are the major children of the deceased Smt. Kempamma.

PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of the Petitioner No.1 to 3 and the deceased and the same are marked at Ex.P.10 to 14.
15.
The PW.1 in her cross-examination admitted that they all are married.

Further she admitted that,
the Petitioner No.2 and 3 are doing agricultural work and they are looking after the welfare of their mother.
Further, she admitted that they did not incur financial loss by the death of their mother.
So it is crystal clear that, the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are not dependents on the income of the deceased.

But, the Petitioners being the children SCCH 15 11 MVC No.3701/2023 of deceased have a right to apply for compensation and it would be bounden duty of the Tribunal to consider the Application irrespective of the fact whether concerned legal representatives were fully dependents on the deceased and not, to limit the claim towards conventional heads only.

As the Petitioners are the LRs of deceased Smt. Kempamma and also they have proved that the death of the Smt. Kempamma has been caused by the rash and negligent driving of the driver of the offending vehicle, they entitled for the compensation.
16. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 53 years and was Homemaker and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
PW.1 has produced Ex.P.13 i.e., the Aadhaar Card of the deceased Smt. Kempamma which shows her date of birth was 01.01.1970.
The alleged accident has been occurred on 25.05.2023.

That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Smt.
Kempamma was 53 years, 4 months and 24 days.
Hence, the age of the deceased Smt. Kempamma to be SCCH 15 12 MVC No.3701/2023 taken at 54 years for the purpose of assessment.
17. In the petition, the age of the deceased was shown as 53 years and the deceased was a Homemaker and was earning Rs.20,000/- per month.
But, PW.1 has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.16,000/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
18. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
19.
The deceased has left behind her, her sons and daughter.
The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are the major sons and married daughter of the deceased.

At this juncture, I would like SCCH 15 13 MVC No.3701/2023 to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that :
Hema vs Anthony Kumar.J on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147122463/
5

entities.text: Special Leave Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others)
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: " Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-, loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".
It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

20. As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are the sons and married daughter of deceased, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/- each towards loss of SCCH 15 14 MVC No.3701/2023 consortium and Rupees 18,150/- towards loss of estate and Rupees 18,150/-
towards funeral expenses.

IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION,
21.
The Petitioner No.1 to 3 being the major children of deceased, they lost their mother's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
22. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
SCCH 15 15 MVC No.3701/2023 VI. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDENCY:

23. As per the discussion made above, the Petitioners are the majors and the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are major sons and married daughter and Petitioner No.2 and 3 are doing agricultural work and they are not the dependents of the deceased.
Hence, the Petitioners are not entitled for any compensation under this head.

24. TOTAL QUANTUM OF COMPENSATION TO WHICH THE PETITIONERS ARE ENTITLED:
1. Loss of consortium Rs.1,45,200/-
2. Loss of Love and Affection Rs. 50,000/-
3. Loss of Estate Rs. 18,150/-
4. Funeral Expenses Rs. 18,150/-
5. Expenses of transportation Rs. 5,000/-
Hema vs Anthony Kumar.J on 12 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/147122463/
6 of dead body 6. Loss of Dependency -

Total Rs.2,36,500/-
 SCCH 15 16 MVC No.3701/2023 Thus, totally the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are awarded compensation of Rs.2,36,500/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

25. Regarding Liability: This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent driving on the part of the driver of the offending Mahindra Bolero bearing Reg.No.KA-10-A-2332.
There is no dispute about the validity of the policy at the time of accident.
In this case, the Respondent No.1 is the owner and Respondent No.2 is the insurer of the offending vehicle.
Therefore, both Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2, who is liable to indemnify the Respondent No.1 has to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 is in the "Affirmative"
and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
SCCH 15 17 MVC No.3701/2023 26. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.2,36,500/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following :
ORDER
The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 and 2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby allowed in part with costs.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.2,36,500/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the  SCCH 15 18 MVC No.3701/2023 insurer, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.
